summary: Penobscot County, ME: Maine Forest Service steel tower built 1919 and abandoned 1970; a rusted hulk lies near the summit, which now has wind turbines.

facts.design: steel lookout tower; heights disputed (see resolved_conflicts)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1970 and cut down a few years later per a 2023 article; the rusted tower lies toppled on its side near the summit per a 2025 guide

staffing.status: fire warden Jesse Harriman, 1923 to 1953 (per a 2023 hiking article)

access.note: A yellow gate on Greenfield Road marks the start; the 2023 article asks visitors not to block it and a 2025 guide calls it locked. No source says whether the summit is open to the public.

visit.trail_note: About two miles one way from the gate along the old Maine Forest Service Jeep road; the ridge now has two communications towers and 13 wind turbines

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 36 feet (1919 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts; Maine Memory), 39 feet (1919 state report quoted by Forest Lookouts) and 30 feet (2023 article). No height_m is recorded because the sources do not agree.
The Forest Fire Lookout Association marks the tower gone; the 2023 article and 2025 guide describe its rusted remains near the summit. The tower is down, but its remains are still on the summit.

notes_for_editor: Height is the main disagreement (30, 36 and 39 feet), so height_m is left unset. Harriman's dates come only from the 2023 article; no archive copy was checked. The 2025 guide says you pass a fire tower on the right and another on the left past the cabin; the sources do not say whether either is a former lookout, so the story does not assume it. Elevation also varies by source (1,463 ft Maine Memory; 1,470 ft Maine by Foot; 1,471 ft CentralMaine), not used. Access: the sources describe a gate and a walk but do not name the owner or say the summit is public. Photo candidates: Maine Memory record 19131 and Maine State Archives item 71; no image URLs were captured, so no photos entries.
